To convert a Digital Object Identifier (DOI) to a BibTeX entry, you can choose between instant web-based converters, command-line tools, or a direct terminal command. [1, 2] Here are the most efficient ways to perform the conversion: ## Method 1: Use a Free Online Converter (Fastest) [3] Several web utilities pull metadata directly from official registries like Crossref to build a clean citation for you. [4] - [doi2bib](https://www.doi2bib.org/): Go to the site, paste your DOI into the input field, and click "Get Citation" to view and copy the output. - [BibTeX.com Copy and paste one or multiple DOIs to process them in bulk and download a .bib file. - [CiteMe App](https://citeme.app/tools/doi-to-bibtex): Paste the DOI or full doi.org URL to retrieve complete author, journal, and page metadata. [1, 3, 5, 6] ## Method 2: Use the Terminal (No Apps Required) [5, 7, 8] If you prefer using your terminal, you can send a cURL request directly to the DOI system. Use a specific header (Accept: application/x-qrcode or text/bibliography; style=bibtex) to force the server to respond with text formatted specifically for BibTeX. [4, 5, 8] Run the following command in your terminal (replace the example DOI with yours): curl -LH "Accept: text/bibliography; style=bibtex" https://doi.org The -L flag ensures that the command follows any server redirects to fetch the correct data. ## Method 3: Reference Managers & Extensions If you manage a large volume of research papers, automating the process through dedicated software prevents manual cluttering: [9] - Zotero: Open the application, click the "Add Item(s) by Identifier" wand icon, paste your DOI, and click Enter. You can then right-click the item and choose "Export Item" as a BibTeX file. - CiteDrive: A web-native bibliography manager where you can navigate to "Search via DOI", paste your identifier, and instantly generate an integrated LaTeX bibliography entry.
